# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** are the best overall pick. They're clip-ons with the clearest sound of the group, and each bud has a physical button, which is easier to use mid-run than touch controls. Runner's World and WIRED both rate them highly. Sale price is about $199 (list $299). Battery is about 7 hours (19.5 with case) and water resistance is only IPX4. Runner's World says Bose plans new open-ear earbuds within about a month, so you may want to wait. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) and [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) list retailer buy buttons.

**Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** is the best bone-conduction option, and it's the one I'd pick if awareness matters most. It has physical buttons, 12 hours of battery and an IP55 rating. WIRED found it has more bass but a bit less clarity than the older OpenRun. The neckband can clash with long hair, high ponytails and winter hats. The list price is $180, with $125 deals shown at REI and Best Buy. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

**Shokz OpenDots 2** ($200) suits long or wet runs. It has 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating, and the top of your ear stays free for hats and sunglasses. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Soundcore AeroFit 2** is the best value hook-style pick. It has IP55 protection, about 10 hours per charge and 42 hours with the case. Prices vary by source:
- SoundGuys shows about $79.99 at Amazon ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)).
- Soundcore's store lists $129.99, or about $104 with code AFSC20, which Dealectric tested on 2026-10-22 ([buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2)). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission if you buy. Check the final price at checkout, since the Amazon price looked lower.

**Nothing Ear (Open)** is SoundGuys' top overall open-ear pick and its best for running. It has strong bass for the category, an IP54 rating and a good EQ app, at about $99 on Amazon. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Budget clip-ons:** the JLab Flex Open (about $40–50) and Soundpeats PearlClip Pro (about $50) are low-risk ways to see if you like open-ear. Expect less bass and detail. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

## Quick guidance
- **Maximum awareness, wet weather, or heavy bass:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.
- **Best sound, easy fit with hats and glasses:** Bose Ultra Open.
- **Long runs or rain:** Shokz OpenDots 2.
- **Tight budget:** Soundcore AeroFit 2, or JLab or Soundpeats if you're only testing the idea.

Open-ear designs leak sound and don't isolate noise, so they're weak in loud gyms. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic. Prices change often, so confirm at checkout.
